# `nlink-lab watch`

## Reference

<!-- cli-ref:start (generated by `nlink-lab docs-gen`; do not edit) -->

```text
Tail nftables + RTNETLINK drift events for a running lab.

Subscribes to every node in the lab and prints one line per kernel mutation — useful for spotting hand-edits that bypass `nlink-lab apply`. `--json` emits NDJSON for piping to `jq`. Plan 159b.

nftables events cover tables, chains, rules, sets, set elements and named objects (counters, quotas, limits); the generation marker the kernel sends after every committed batch is not shown. Elements a rule adds from the packet path (`add @set`) are not notified by the kernel.

Each event is nlink's view of the object: a line such as `[r1/route] new_link ifindex=7 mtu=1500 name=d0 …`, and with `--json` a record such as `{"node":"r1","family":"route","kind":"event","event":{"object":"link","action":"new",…}}`. The event's name, `<action>_<object>`, is what `events --kind` filters drift on.

A node whose stream ends prints `watch ended: <error>` (an `ended` record in `--json`) and is subscribed again after a backoff; one whose namespace is gone, or was replaced by a redeploy of the lab, prints `namespace gone` (`gone`) and stops. The command exits when every node's watch has stopped, or when its output is closed.

Every change is shown, whoever made it: what a concurrent `apply`, `impair`, `node`, `link` or `node restart` does prints like a hand edit.

Usage: nlink-lab watch [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -L, --lab <LAB>
          The lab. Default: `$NLINK_LAB`, then the one `nlink-lab use` selected, then the only running lab

      --family <FAMILY>
          Event family: route, nftables, or both
          
          [default: both]
          [possible values: route, nftables, both]

      --node <NODE>
          Restrict subscription to a single node. Without this flag, every node in the lab is subscribed. Filter is pre-subscription — we don't open connections we don't need

      --include-snapshot
          Show resync replay frames after ENOBUFS recoveries. By default they're silenced — the user only sees live multicast deltas. With this flag, snapshot frames render with a `[snapshot]` marker

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

<!-- cli-ref:end -->
